G7501.definition: a prop, stay, support , Lat. columen, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural the props  to keep a boat on shore upright, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7505.definition:
a day-labourer, hired servant  of any sort; in (Iliad by Homer), ἔριθοι are mowers  or reapers : later, ἔριθοι, αἱ, spinsters, workers in wool , (Demosthenes Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7508.definition: 1. to creep, crawl , Lat. serpo, repo, and generally to move slowly, walk , (Homer); of reports, to creep on, spread , like Lat. serpit rumor, (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ πόλεμος ἑρπέτω let  it take its course , (Aristophanes Comicus); of calamities, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7509.definition: a redness on the skin , (Thucydides); ἐρ. προσώπου a blush , (Euripides):—;absolute redness , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7512.definition: the heron  or hern , Lat. ardea, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7513.definition:
1. love , [variant datesTragica Adespota:—; love of  a thing, desire for  it, τινός (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural loves, amours , (Euripides); in (Sophocles Tragicus), of passionate joy , compare φρίσσω II. 3. 
2. as proper noun the god of love, Eros, Amor , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

 (AS)

G7516.definition:
1. the hearth, fire-place , (Homer); the sanctuary of suppliants, καθέζετο ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάρῃ ἐν κονίῃσιν (Odyssey by Homer):—; a pan of coals, a brasier , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. πυρὸς ἐσχάραι the watch-fires  of the camp, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. an altar for burnt-offerings , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7522.definition:
1. a companion , (Iliad by Homer); φόρμιγξ, ἣν δαιτὶ θεοὶ ποίησαν ἑταίρην (Odyssey by Homer); πενία σφιν ἑταίρα (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. opposite to a lawful wife, a concubine, a courtesan , (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

G7526.definition: coupled with an animal of diverse kind , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G7528.definition: easy to be taken  or caught , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7529.definition:
1. well-joined, harmonious , (Euripides) 
2. of men, accommodating , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7530.definition:
1. adverb well, rightly , to confirm or approve what has been said, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;ironically, (Euripides) 
2. without a Verb, good! well said! well done! bravo!  Lat. euge! (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7531.definition: nobility of birth, high descent , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὐγένεια παίδων = εὐγενεῖς παῖδες, (Euripides) (ML)

G7532.definition:
1. well-known, familiar , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. easy to discern , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7533.definition: to be of good repute, to be held in esteem, honoured, famous, popular , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.: —; εὐδ. ἔν τινι to be distinguished  in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπί τινι (Plato Philosophus):—; εὐδ. παρὰ τῷ βασιλέϊ to have influence  with him, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7535.definition: of good hope, hopeful, cheerful, sanguine , (Thucydides), etc.:—;with infinitive future, εὔελπις ἰσχύσειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔελπις σωθήσεσθαι in good hope  to be saved, (Thucydides) (ML)

G7536.definition:
1. well-girdled , of women, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. of men, girt up for exercise, dressed for walking, active , (Horace)'s alte praecinctus , (Herdotus Historicus); of light troops, unincumbered , Lat. expeditus, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. metaphorically unincumbered , πενία (Plutarch) (ML)

G7541.definition:
1. to thrive, flourish, prosper , Lat. florere, vigere, (Herdotus Historicus):—;with dative to abound in  a thing, (Homeric Hymns) 
2. Pass. in same sense, οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι εὐθηνήθησαν (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν εὐθενεῖσθαι (Demosthenes Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7546.definition: easy to be despised, contemptible, despicable , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7547.definition: of good report, famous, glorious , (Homer), etc.; εὐκλεέστατος βίος (Euripides) adverb -εῶς, epic -ειῶς, (Iliad by Homer); κατθανεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); Sup. εὐκλεέστατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7549.definition:
1. of persons, easily satisfied, contented with one's food , [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Plutarch) 
2. easily satisfied, contented, good-natured, peaceable , Lat. facilis, comis, (Aristophanes Comicus); with dative, εὔκολος πολίταις friendly  to them, at peace with  them, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb -λως, tranquilly, calmly , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. willing, agile , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. in bad sense, easily led, prone , πρὸς ἀδικίαν (Lucian) 
5. of things, easy , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7550.definition:
1. sweetly-speaking , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. = εὔγλωσσος II, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7551.definition: of good size, very large , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7553.definition: of a good length, tall , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7554.definition: easy to pass , of mountains, (Xenophon Historicus); of a road, easy to travel , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7556.definition:
to be well off, enjoy oneself, make merry , (Herdotus Historicus) 
from εὐπᾶθής (ML)

G7557.definition:
1. with fine purple border , (Plutarch) 
2. of persons, wearing such a garment , Lat. praetextatus, a grandee, (Lucian) (ML)

G7558.definition:
1. well-looking, goodly, comely , of outward appearance, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; εὐπρ. ἰδεῖν fair  to look on, (Xenophon Historicus); εἶδος εὐπρεπής (Euripides) 
2. decent, seemly, fitting, becoming , (Herdotus Historicus); τελευτὴ εὐπρεπεστάτη a most glorious  end, (Thucydides) 
3. specious, plausible , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς in pretence , (Thucydides) 
4. adverb -πῶς, ionic πέως, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; comparative -πέστερον, (Euripides); Sup. -πέστατα, (Thucydides) (ML)

G7559.definition:
1. fair of face , (Aristophanes Comicus): with glad countenance , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically fair in outward show, specious , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7561.definition:
1. an invention, discovery , (Euripides), etc. 
2. with genitive an invention, for  or against  a thing, a remedy , (Euripides) 
3. that which is found unexpectedly , i. e., much like Ἕρμαιον, a piece of good luck, godsend, windfall, prize , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
4. of a child, a foundling , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7563.definition: breadth, width , absolute, εὖρος in breadth , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; so, τὸ εὖρος (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς εὖρος (Euripides) (ML)

G7564.definition:
1. wide, broad , (Homer), etc. 
2. far-reaching, far-spread , κλέος εὐρύ (Odyssey by Homer); ἐλπίδες [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. as adverb the neuter εὐρύ is mostly used, (Iliad by Homer), etc. (ML)

G7565.definition: to be  or become mouldy , βίος εὐρωτιῶν the life of the unwashed , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7567.definition:
to be steady, favourable , (Euripides):—; to be calm, tranquil , of the sea, (Lucian) 
from εὐστᾶθής (ML)

G7572.definition:
1. easily handled, easy to deal with, easy , εὐχερές ἐστι, with infinitive, (Batrachomyomachia); πάντα ταῦτ᾽ ἐν εὐχερεῖ ἔθου didst make light  of them, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb -ρῶς, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of persons, manageable, accommodating, kind, yielding , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb, εὐχερῶς φέρειν (Plato Philosophus), etc.; comparative -έστερον, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in bad sense, unscrupulous, reckless , (Demosthenes Orator):—;adverb -ρῶς, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7579.definition:
1. to bind on  or to , λύουσα ἢ ' φάπτουσα undoing or making fast , (Sophocles Tragicus); τοὖργον ὡς ἐφάψειεν τόδε that she had made fast  (i. e. perpetrated) the deed, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., 3rd singular perfect and pluperfect ἐφῆπται, -το, is  or was hung over  one, impends over, is fixed as  one's doom , with dative, Τρώεσσι κήδεe ἐφῆπται (Iliad by Homer) 
2. Mid. to lay hold of, grasp, reach , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. to lay hold of  with the mind, attain to , Lat. assequi, with genitive, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. in (Pindar) also with dative (like θιγγάνω, ψαύω); to apply oneself to.  
5. (Herdotus Historicus) uses participle perfect passive with genitive, εἴδεος ἐπαμμένος possessed of  a certain degree of beauty. 
6. to follow, come next , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7580.definition:
1. to draw on, drag  or trail after  one, ἐπ. τὰς οὐράς, of long-tailed sheep, (Herdotus Historicus); ἵππον ἐκ τοῦ βραχίονος ἐπ. to lead  a horse by a rein upon the arm, (Herdotus Historicus); ναῦς ὡς ἐφέλξω will take in tow , (Euripides) 
2. to bring on, bring in its train , (Euripides) 
3. to drink off , (Euripides) 
4. Pass., ἐφελκομένοισι πόδεσσι with feet trailing after  him, of one who is dragged lifeless away, (Iliad by Homer); ἐφέλκετο ἔγχος, i. e. sticking in his hand, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπελκόμενος trailing behind , of a boat, (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ἐπελκόμενοι the stragglers  of an army, (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to be attracted , (Homeric Hymns) 
6. Mid. to draw to oneself, attract , αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐφέλκεται ἄνδρα σίδηρος the very sight of arms attracts  men, i. e. tempts  them to use it , (Odyssey by Homer) 
7. to draw  or pull over , (Plutarch); ἐφ. ὀφρῦς to frown, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
8. to bring on  consequences, (Euripides) 
9. to assume , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7582.definition:
1. boiled, dressed , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. ἑφθὸς χρυσός refined  gold, (Simonides Lyricus) (ML)

G7583.definition:
1. to visit, go the rounds, patrol , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., ἐφοδεύεται the rounds are made , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. with dative to watch over , ἀγῶσιν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7584.definition:
1. to furnish with supplies for a journey , Lat. viaticum dare, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. Mid., πενταδραχμίαν ἑκάστῳ ἐφοδιασάμενος having seen  that five drachms were paid  to each, (Xenophon Historicus):—;metaphorically to maintain , ἀργίαν (Plutarch) (ML)

G7586.definition:
1. to oversee, observe, survey , of the sun, (Homer):—;then of the gods, to watch over, observe, take notice of , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; of a general going his rounds, (Thucydides); to visit  the sick, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. simply, to look upon, view, behold , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., ὅσον ἐφεωρᾶτο τῆς νήσου as much of it as was in view , (Thucydides) 
3. to look out, choose , ἐπιόψομαι ἥτις ἀρίστη (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G7591.definition:
1. the urchin, hedgehog , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. the sea-urchin , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. the shell of the sea-urchin , often used as a cup : then like Lat. testa, a pot, jug, pitcher, Lat. echinus, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—; the vase  in which the notes of evidence were deposited, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. in plural sharp points  at each end of a bit, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7594.definition:
1. to boil, seethe , (Herdotus Historicus), attic: proverbial of useless labour, λίθον ἕψεις (Aristophanes Comicus); with genitive partitive, ἥψομεν τοῦ κορκόρου we boiled some  pimpernel, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be boiled , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of metals, to smelt, refine , (Pindar) 
3. metaphorically, γῆρας ἀνώνυμον ἕψειν to cherish  an inglorious age, (Pindar) (ML)

G7595.definition: in the morning, early , (Herdotus Historicus): —; τὸ ἑωθινόν, as adverb, early in the morning , (Herdotus Historicus); so, ἐξ ἑωθινοῦ = ἕωθεν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7599.definition:
1. to yoke, put to , ἵππους (Homer), etc.; ζ. ἵππους ὑφ᾽ ἅρματα, ὑφ᾽ ἅρμασιν, ὑπ᾽ ὄχεσφιν, ὑπ᾽ ἀμάξηισιν (Iliad by Homer);—;(so in Mid., ἵππους ζεύγνυσθαι to put to one's  horses, (Homer));—;also of riding horses, to harness, saddle and bridle , ζεῦξαι Πάγασον (Pindar):—;of chariots, to put to, get ready , (Homer) 
2. to bind, bind fast , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., φάρη ἐζευγμέναι having  them fastened , (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically, πότμωι ζυγείς in the yoke of  fate, (Pindar); ἀνάγκηι, ὁρκίοις ζυγείς (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to join together , σανίδες ἐζευγμέναι well-joined , (Iliad by Homer) 
5. to join in wedlock , (Euripides):—;in Mid., of the husband, to wed , (Euripides):—;Pass. to be married , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. to join  opposite banks by bridges , τὸν Ἑλλήσποντον ζεῦξαι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;also, γέφυραν ζεῦξαι to form  a bridge, (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. to undergird  ships with ropes , (Thucydides) (ML)

G7602.definition:
1. to be emulated, worthy of imitation , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to be deemed happy, to be envied , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 
3. of conditions, enviable, blessed , (Euripides) (ML)

G7605.definition: to yoke together , ζ. κιθάραν to put the cross-bar to  the lyre, (Lucian) (ML)

G7609.definition: to paint from life, to paint , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7611.definition: Lat. jus, sauce to eat with meat, fish, etc., (Aristophanes Comicus); ὁ μέλας ζ. the black broth  of Spartans, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7614.definition: to kindle into flame, light up : metaphorically, ζ. τάρβος (Aeschulus Tragicus); νείκη (Euripides) (ML)

G7616.definition:
1. ready to lead  or guide , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. fit to command, authoritative, leading , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3. = Rom. Consularis , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7618.definition:
1. one must lead , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. one must suppose , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7619.definition: to sweeten, season, give a flavour  or relish to  a thing, with accusative, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7620.definition:
1. sweet  to the taste or smell, (Homer); to the hearing, (Homer); then of any pleasant  feeling or state, as sleep, (Homer):—;with infinitive, ἡδὺς δρακεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡδὺς ἀκοῦσαι λόγος (Plato Philosophus):—; ἡδύ ἐστι or γίγνεται it is pleasant , (Homer), etc.:—;so, οὔ μοι ἥδιόν ἐστι λέγειν I had rather not say, (Herdotus Historicus):—;neuter as Substantive, τὰ ἡδέα pleasures , (Thucydides):—;neuter as adverb, sweetly , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. after (Homer), of persons, pleasant, welcome , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. well-pleased, glad , (Sophocles Tragicus); in addressing a person, ὦ ἥδιστε, Horace's dulcissime rerum , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. like εὐήθης, innocent, simple , ὡς ἡδὺς εἶ (Plato Philosophus) 
5. adverb ἡδέως, sweetly, pleasantly, with pleasure , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ἡδέως ἂν ἐροίμην I would gladly  ask, should like to ask, (Demosthenes Orator);—; ἡδ. ἔχειν τι to be pleased  or content  with, (Euripides); ἡδ. ἔχειν πρός τινα or τινί to be kind, well-disposed  to one, (Demosthenes Orator):—; comparative ἥδιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Sup., ἥδιστα (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7621.definition: that which gives a relish  or flavour, seasoning, sauce , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G7626.definition:
electron , a word sometimes used to denote amber , as probably in (Homer) and (Herdotus Historicus);—;sometimes pale gold , a compound of 1 part of silver to 4 of gold, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.—;In (Aristophanes Comicus) ἐκπιπτουσῶν τῶν ἠλέκτρων, the ἤλεκτροι are probably the pegs of the lyre made of  or inlaid with electron.  
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7627.definition: Dep.:—; to sit in the court  Ἡλιαία, be a Heliast , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7629.definition:
1. a half-ass , i. e. a mule , (Homer), etc.:—; proverbial, ἐπεὰν ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, i. e. never, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the ἡμ. ἀγροτέρα of (Iliad by Homer) 2. 851 is probably the wild ass.  
3. as adjective, βρέφος ἡμίονον a mule- foal, (Iliad by Homer); ἡμ. βασιλεύς a mule- king, half-Mede half-Persian, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7633.definition:
1. one who holds the reins, a driver, charioteer , opposite to παραιβάτης (the warrior by his side), (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally a chariot-driver , as in the games, (Pindar), attic:—;in (Theognis Elegiacus), a rider.  
3. metaphorically a guide, governor , (Pindar) (ML)

G7634.definition: the liver , (Homer), etc.:—; ὑφ᾽ ἥπατος φέρειν, of pregnant  women, (Euripides):—;in [variant datesTragica Adespota as the seat of the passions, anger, fear, etc., answering therefore to our heart. (ML)

G7636.definition:
1. a hero, in (Homer) used of the Greeks before Troy, then of warriors  generally; and then of all free men of the heroic age, as the minstrel Demodocus, the herald Mulius, even the unwarlike Phaeacians. 
2. in (Hesiod) the blessed heroes  are the fourth age of men, who fell before Thebes and Troy, and then passed to the Islands of the Blest. 
3. heroes, as objects of worship, demigods  or men born from a god and a mortal, as Hercules, Aeneas, Memnon, (Herdotus Historicus); then of such as had done great services to mankind, as Daedalus, Triptolemus, Theseus, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. later, the heroes are inferior local deities , patrons of tribes, cities, guilds, founders of cities, etc.; as at Athens, the ἥρωες ἐπώνυμοι were the heroes after whom the  φυλαί were named , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7637.definition: stilly, quietly, softly, gently , (Pindar); ἔχ᾽ ἡσυχῆ keep quiet , (Plato Philosophus); ἡς. γελάσαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7638.definition:
1. a sound , but properly of a returned sound, echo , (Homeric Hymns), etc. 
2. generally, a ringing sound , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7639.definition:
1. to bloom, abound, to be luxuriant , of fruit-trees, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; often in participle perfect τεθηλώς, epic feminine τεθαλυῖα, as adjective, luxuriant, exuberant , (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate, οὐ δένδρε᾽ ἔθαλλεν χῶρος the place grew  no trees, θαλλούσης βίον ἐλαίας (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of other natural objects, τεθαλυῖα ἐέρση the fresh  or copious  dew, (Odyssey by Homer); τεθαλυῖα ἀλοιφῆι rich  with fat, (Iliad by Homer); εἰλαπίνηι τεθαλυίηι at a sumptuous  feast, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. of men, to bloom, flourish , (Hesiod), etc. 
4. in bad sense, to be active , νόσος ἀεὶ τέθηλε (Sophocles Tragicus); πήματα ἀεὶ θάλλοντα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7654.definition: feminine of θεράπων, a waiting maid, handmaid , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7656.definition: a hunter, huntsman , (Iliad by Homer); κυσὶ θηρευτῇσι (Iliad by Homer); also of a fisher , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7661.definition:
1. hot, warm , θερμὰ λοετρά (Homer); of tears, (Homer), etc. 
2. metaphorically hot, hasty, rash, headlong , like Lat. calidus, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. still warm, fresh , ἴχνη [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. τὸ θερμόν = θερμότης, heat , Lat. calor, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5. θερμόν (i.e. ὕδωρ); hot water , θερμῷ λοῦσθαι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. τὰ θερμά (entry χωρία); (Herdotus Historicus): but (entry λουτρά); hot baths , (Xenophon Historicus) 
7. adverb -μῶς, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7662.definition:
1. a setting, placing, arranging , (Pindar); θ. νόμων lawgiving , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a deposit  of money, preparatory to a law-suit, (Aristophanes Comicus): money paid in advance, earnest-money , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. position, situation , Lat. situs, of a city, (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G7663.definition:
1. like θέμις, that which is laid down and established, a law, ordinance , Lat. institutum, λέκτροιο θεσμὸν ἵκοντο, i. e. they fulfilled the established law  of wedlock, (Odyssey by Homer); so in (Herdotus Historicus) and attic 
2. at Athens, Draco's laws were called θεσμοί, because each began with the word θεσμός (compare θεσμοθέτης); while (Solon Lyricus)'s laws were named νόμοι. 
3. an institution, ordinance , as the court of Areopagus, (Aeschulus Tragicus); of the great games, (Pindar) (ML)

G7668.definition:
1. a wild beast, beast of prey , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; joined with λέων, (Euripides); with λέαινα, [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also of Cerberus, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural beasts , as opposite to birds and fishes, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
2. of any animal , as of birds, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. any fabulous monster , as the sphinx, (Aeschulus Tragicus); especially a centaur , (Sophocles Tragicus) (compare Φήρ)); a satyr , (Euripides) (ML)

G7672.definition:
a store, treasure , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
from θησαυρίζω (ML)

G7674.definition:
1. a band  or company marching through the streets with dance and song , especially in honour of Bacchus, a band of revellers , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. generally, any party, company, troop , (Euripides) (ML)

G7676.definition:
1. a heap , (Odyssey by Homer):—;in plural sand-heaps, sand-bank , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. the beach, shore , παρὰ θῖνα θαλάσσης (Iliad by Homer); παρὰ θῖν᾽ ἁλός (Iliad by Homer); so, ἐπὶ θινί (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. sand  or mud  at the bottom of the sea, οἶδμα κυλίνδει βυσσόθεν θῖνα (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically, τὸν θῖνά μου ταράττεις you trouble the very bottom  of my heart, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7682.definition:

G7683.definition:

G7694.definition: an African tree with scented wood , a kind of juniper  or cedar , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G7696.definition:

G7697.definition:

G7708.definition: the ibis , an Egyptian bird, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7709.definition: the part behind the thigh and knee, the ham , Lat. poples, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7711.definition:
1. to make to sit down, to seat , (Homer), etc.; αὐτός τε κάθησο καὶ ἄλλους ἵδρυε λαούς (Iliad by Homer); ἵδρυσε τὴν στρατιήν encamped  the army, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be seated, sit. still , (Iliad by Homer); of an army, to lie encamped , (Herdotus Historicus); ἀσφαλῶς ἱδρυμένος seated, steady, secure , (Herdotus Historicus)

G7732.definition: any web, a sail , ἱστία στέλλεσθαι, μηρύεσθαι, καθελεῖν to lower or furl sail , (Odyssey by Homer); ἄκροισι χρῆσθαι ἱστίοις to keep the sails  close-reefed, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7733.definition:

G7766.definition: to be fast asleep, fall asleep , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., perfect participle κατυπνωμένος asleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

2. the crown  or top of the head , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
3. the top  or peak  of a mountain, (Iliad by Homer) 
4. metaphorically the highest point , Lat. summa, παντὸς ἔχει κορυφάν is the best of all , (Pindar); κορυφὰ λόγων προτέρων the sum and substance  of ancient legends, (Pindar) 
5. the height  or excellence of  a thing, i. e. the choicest, noblest, best , (Pindar) 
 (ML)

G8074.definition:
1. Lat. cornix, the chough or sea-crow , a small kind with red legs and bill, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. = κόραξ, the carrion-crow , (Hesiod) 
3. anything hooked  or curved , like a crow's bill, 
4. the handle on a door , (Odyssey by Homer) 
5. the tip of a bow , on which the bowstring was hooked, (Homer):—;metaphorically, βιῷ κορώνην ἐπιθεῖναι to put a finish  to life, (Lucian) (ML)

G8077.definition:
1. a cup , (Homer) 
2. the cup  or socket  of a joint, especially of the hip-joint, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. a liquid measure , containing 6 κύαθοι, i. e. nearly half a pint , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8078.definition:
1. a shearing  or cropping  of the hair, tonsure , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a lock cut off , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8079.definition: a barber, hair-cutter , Lat. tonsor, [5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina, etc. (ML)

G8080.definition:
1. light, nimble , [variant datesTragica Adespota; used by (Homer) only in neuter plural as. adverb κοῦφα προβιβάς stepping lightly on, (Iliad by Homer):—;metaphorically, κουφότεραι φρένες too buoyant , (Pindar) 
2. metaphorically also light, easy , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. empty, unsubstantial, vain , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. light  in point of weight, opposite to βαρύς, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνωθε πέσοι may earth lie lightly  on thee, sit tibi terra levis , (Euripides); of soldiers, ὡπλισμένοι κουφοτέροις ὅπλοις (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. adverb -φως, lightly, nimbly , (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. ἐσκευασμένοι, of soldiers, (Thucydides) 
6. metaphorically lightly, with light heart , κουφότερόν μετεφώνεε (Odyssey by Homer); κούφως φέρειν to bear lightly , (Euripides); ὡς κουφότατα φέρειν (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. lightly, with ease , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8083.definition: only in present, to have a sick head-ache , consequent upon a debauch, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8089.definition:
1. a mixing vessel , especially a large bowl, in which the wine was mixed with water , and from which the cups were filled, (Homer), etc.; οἶνον δ᾽ ἐκ κρητῆρος ἀφυσσάμενοι δεπάεσσιν ἔκχεον (Iliad by Homer); πίνοντες κρητῆρας drinking bowls of wine , (Iliad by Homer); κρητῆρα στήσασθαι ἐλεύθερον to give a bowl of wine  to be drunk in honour of the deliverance, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπιστέψασθαι ποτοῖο, see. ἐπιστέφω. 
2. metaphorically, κρατῆρα πλήσας κακῶν having filled a bowl  full of woes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. any cup-shaped hollow, a basin  in a rock, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8090.definition: a flesh-hook , to take meat out of the pot, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8091.definition: to distribute flesh, to divide the flesh  of a victim among the guests, (Lucian):—;Mid. to divide among themselves , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8092.definition: hung, hung up, hanging , κρ. αὐχένος hung by  the neck, (Sophocles Tragicus); with genitive, also, hung from  or on  a thing, (Euripides): —; κρεμαστὴ ἀρτάνη, i. e. a halter, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, βρόχοι κρ. (Euripides) (ML)

G8093.definition: a well, spring, fountain , Lat. fons, (Homer), etc.; opposite to φρέαρ (a tank), (Herdotus Historicus): —;Poets use it in plural for water , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8094.definition:
1. a half-boot , (Xenophon Historicus):—; κρηπῖδες soldiers' boots , i. e. soldiers  themselves, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. generally, a groundwork, foundation, basement  of a temple or altar, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, κρηπὶς σοφῶν ἐπέων (Pindar); οὐδέπω κρηπὶς κακῶν ὕπεστι we have not yet got to the bottom  of misery, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ ἐγκράτεια ἀρετῆς κρηπίς self-control is the foundation  of virtue, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. the walled edge  of a river, a quay , Lat. crepido, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8095.definition:
1. a ring  on a horse's breast-band, to fasten it to the peg  ἕστωρ); at the end of the carriage-pole, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. an eyelet-hole  in sails, through which the reefing-ropes were drawn, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8096.definition:
1. a ram , Lat. aries, (Homer), etc. 
2. a battering-ram , Lat. aries, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8097.definition:
1. the thread which is passed between the threads of the warp  στήμων, tela ), the woof  or weft , Lat. subtemen, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. κροκύς, the flock  or nap of woollen cloth, cloth with curly nap , (Aristophanes Comicus): in plural, μαλακαῖς κρόκαις with cloths of  soft wool , (Pindar); κρόκαισι with flocks of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8098.definition:
1. a lizard , properly an ionic word, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the Nile-lizard, crocodile , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8099.definition:
1. the crocus , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. saffron  (which is made from its stigmas), (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G8103.definition:
1. the side of the forehead  (see. κόρση); in plural the temples , Lat. tempora, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of a mountain, its side , [6th/5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G8104.definition:
1. to make to rattle , of horses, ὄχεα κροτέοντες rattling  them along , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to knock, strike, smite , (Herdotus Historicus); κροτεῖν τὰς χεῖρας or τὼ χεῖρε to clap  the hands, (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to clap, applaud , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3. of a smith, to hammer  or weld together , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be wrought by the hammer ; metaphorically, ἐξ ἀπάτας κεκροταμένος one mass  of trickery, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
4. intransitive to make a rattling noise , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8107.definition:
1. hidden, concealed , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
2. secret, clandestine , (Hesiod), etc. (ML)

G8108.definition: to kill, slay , (Homer), etc.; of animals, to slaughter , (Homer); Οὖτις με κτείνει δόλωι seeks to kill  me (the force of the present tense), (Odyssey by Homer); ὁ κτανών the slayer, murderer , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οἱ κτανόντες (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; to put to death  by law, (Thucydides)—;In attic θνήσκω or ἀποθνήσκω is used for the Pass. (ML)

G8111.definition:
1. acquisition , (Thucydides); κατ᾽ ἔργου κτῆσιν according to success in  the work, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. (from perfect) possession , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
3. as collective, = κτήματα, possessions, property , (Homer); in plural, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8112.definition:
1. a cup , for drawing wine out of the κρατήρ or bowl, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2. a cupping-glass , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8113.definition:
1. a bean , Lat. faba, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the lot  by which public officers were elected at Athens (because those who drew white beans  were chosen), ὁ τῷ κυάμῳ λαχών an officer chosen by lot , (Herdotus Historicus); βουλὴ ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ κυάμου (Thucydides); ἄρχοντας ἀπὸ κυάμου καθιστάναι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8114.definition:
1. Lat. gubernare, to steer, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.: absolute to act as pilot  or helmsman , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. metaphorically to guide, govern , (Pindar) (ML)

G8115.definition:
1. Lat. cubus, a cube: a cubical die, marked on all 6 sides (whereas the ἀστράγαλος was marked only on four sides), in plural, dice , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; the Greeks threw with three  dice, so that τρὶς ἕξ, three sixes, was the highest throw, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κρίνειν τι ἐν κύβοις to decide it by the dice , by chance , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. also of the single pips on the dice , βέβληκ᾽ Ἀχιλλεὺς δύο κύβω καὶ τέσσαρα he has thrown two aces  and a four, (Aeschulus Tragicus) quoted in (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. a cubic number , i. e. a number multiplied twice into itself, as 27 is the cube of 3, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8116.definition:
the din of battle, uproar, hubbub , (Iliad by Homer) 
Formed from the sound. (ML)

G8117.definition: glory, renown , especially in war, (Iliad by Homer): of a single person, κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν glory  of the Achaians, like Lat. decus, (Homer) (ML)

G8120.definition: a swan , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;metaphorically, from the legends of the swan's dying song ( (Aeschulus Tragicus)), a minstrel , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8121.definition:
1. to rise in waves  or billows, to swell , (Homer) 
2. metaphorically of passion, to swell, seethe , (Pindar) 
3. transitive to agitate , (Lucian) (ML)

G8124.definition: to hunt, chase , later form of κυνηγετέω, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8126.definition:
1. dog-like , Lat. caninus, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Κυνικός, οῦ, a Cynic , as the followers of the philosopher Antisthenes were called, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8129.definition:
of cypress-wood , (Odyssey by Homer) 
from κῦπάρισσος (ML)

G8133.definition: curved, arched , of a wave breaking, (Iliad by Homer); ὤμω κυρτώ round, humped , (Iliad by Homer); κ. τροχός (Euripides) (ML)

G8134.definition:
1. the hollow  of a shield or breastplate, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. any vessel, a vase, jar, urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πλεκτὸν κ. a basket, (Euripides) 
3. anything that contains the body , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8136.definition: any hollow vessel: a chest, box , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8137.definition:
1. in present and imperfect, of females, to conceive , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. rarely with accusative to be pregnant with  a child, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in aor1 ἔκυ_σα, Causal, of the male, to impregnate , and middle ἐκυ_σάμην, of the female, to conceive , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8138.definition: a bell , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in fortified towns an officer went round at night with a bell to challenge the sentries, and see that they were awake, (Thucydides); ὡς κώδωνα ἐξαψάμενος like one with an alarm-bell  in his hand, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8142.definition:
1. a hindrance, impediment , (Euripides) 
2. a defence against  a thing, precaution , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8143.definition: the head man of a village , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8144.definition:
1. any handle: 
2. the handle of an oar , and generally an oar , (Odyssey by Homer), attic; νερτέρᾳ προσήμενος κώπῃ, = θαλαμίτης, metaphorically of a man of low rank, (Aeschulus Tragicus); παραπέμπειν ἐφ᾽ ἕνδεκα κώπαις, a proverb of dubious origin, meaning to escort with all the honours,  (Aristophanes Comicus):—;poetry to express ships, σὺν κώπᾳ χιλιοναύτᾳ, of Agamemnon's fleet, (Euripides) 
3. the handle of a sword, the haft, hilt , Lat. capulus, (Homer) 
4. the handle of a key , (Odyssey by Homer) 
5. the haft of a torch , (Euripides) (ML)

G8148.definition:
1. the part intended for grasping, a handle, haft , (Demosthenes Orator); λαβαὶ ἀμφίστομοι of a cup, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. as a pugilistic term, a grip  or hold , ὥσπερ ἀθλητὴς λαβὴν ζητεῖν (Plutarch):—;metaphorically a handle, occasion, opportunity , λαβὴν διδόναι, Lat. ausam praebere, (Aristophanes Comicus); so, λ. παραδιδόναι, παρέχειν (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8150.definition:
1. (Homer) of wind, rain, etc., furious, boisterous , (Herdotus Historicus); λ. πῦρ, κύματα, πόντος, etc., (Euripides) 
2. after (Homer), of men, boisterous, turbulent, violent , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 
3. greedy , (Pindar) 
4. adverb λάβρως, violently, furiously , (Theognis Elegiacus) 
5. greedily , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8153.definition: neuterplural as adverb, treacherously , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8154.definition:
1. a pond  for water-fowl, Lat. vivarium, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a pit, reservoir , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8155.definition:
1. talk, prattle , (Moschus Bucolicus) 
2. a prater , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8157.definition:
1. a small torch , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. a bandage  for wounds, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8160.definition:
1. a stand  or grate  for pine and other wood used for lighting rooms , (Odyssey by Homer); ὧ χαῖρε, λ. νυκτός thou that lightest up  the night, of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἕσπεροι λαμπτῆρες the evening watch-fires , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. generally, = λαμπάς 1 (Euripides) (ML)

G8162.definition: to hew in stone , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G8163.definition:
1. to lap with the tongue , of wolves, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to drink greedily, suck in , (Lucian) (ML)

G8164.definition:
1. a ravenous sea-bird, perhaps a cormorant , described as dashing down into the sea and then floating on the waves, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically of demagogues, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a singing bird, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8168.definition: spoils  taken in war, Lat. spolia, [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8171.definition:
1. to smooth  or polish , (Homer); ἵπποισι κέλευθον λειανέω I will smooth  the way, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to rub smooth, pound in a mortar , Lat. levigare, (Herdotus Historicus); to grind  with the teeth, (Xenophon Historicus):—; generally, to crush, extirpate , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to smooth away  wrinkles, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically to smooth  or soften down  harsh words, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8172.definition:
1. a kettle  or caldron  of copper, (Homer), etc. 
2. a basin  in which the purifying water  χέρνιψ); was handed to the guests before meals, (Odyssey by Homer); also a pan  for washing the feet, (Odyssey by Homer): a bath , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. a cymbal , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. a cinerary urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally, a casket , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8175.definition: a tree-moss, lichen , then, a lichenlike eruption, canker, scurvy, blight , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8176.definition:
1. to lick up , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. irregular participle perfect, γλώσσηισι λελειχμότες playing with  their tongues, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8178.definition:
1. a speaking, saying, speech , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. a way of speaking, diction, style , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. κατὰ λέξιν as the phrase goes , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8183.definition: to make small  or fine: to thresh out, winnow , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be reduced, grow lean , (Aristotle Philosopher); τοὺς ὤμους λεπτύνεσθαι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8185.definition:
1. a place where people assembled to talk and hear news, a lounge, club-room , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.: —;also a council-hall, council , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. talk  or gossip , such as went on in the λέσχαι, (Euripides):—; in good sense, conversation, discussion , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8186.definition: to have white blossoms : generally, to be white  or made white , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8187.definition:
1. white leprosy , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. the white poplar , Lat. populus alba, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8189.definition: anything received, income , (Aeschulus Tragicus); λ. καὶ ἀνάλωμα receipt  and expense, (Plato Philosophus): generally, gain, profit , Lat. lucrum, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; παντὸς ἥττων λήμματος unable to resist any temptation of gain , (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8192.definition:
to turn into stone, petrify , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
from λῖθουργός (ML)

G8198.definition: to kill by hunger, starve , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8199.definition: to be famished, hungry , [Refs 1st c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8200.definition: of flax, flaxen, linen , Lat. lineus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8202.definition:
1. to oil, anoint : Mid. to anoint oneself , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. of rivers, to make fat, enrich , (Euripides) (ML)

G8204.definition:
1. to beg, pray, entreat, beseech , either absolute or with accusative pers., (Homer); that by which  one prays, in genitive, λ. τινα γούνων (Iliad by Homer); λ. Ζηνός (Odyssey by Homer):—;an infinitive is often added, οὐδέ ς᾽ ἔγωγε λίσσομαι μένειν I do not pray  thee to remain, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. with accusative rei, to beg  or pray for , οἷ αὐτῶι θάνατον λιτέσθαι (Iliad by Homer): with double accusative of persons or things, ταῦτα μὲν οὐχ ὑμέας ἔτι λίσσομαι this I beg  of you no more, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8205.definition: to pray, entreat , especially for protection, either absolute or with accusative pers., (Homer); that by which  one prays in genitive, γούνων λιτανεύειν (Odyssey by Homer); also, γούνων ἁψάμενοι λιτανεύσομεν (epic for -ωμεν); (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8206.definition:
1. smooth, plain : of style, simple, unadorned , (Aristotle Philosopher): of persons, simple, frugal , (Polybius Historicus): adverb λιτῶς, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. paltry, petty , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8207.definition:
1. the lobe of the ear , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the lobe of the liver , (Aeschulus Tragicus): generally, the liver , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8212.definition:
1. the mane  on the neck and back of certain animals, the mane  of horses, the bristly back  of boars and hyaenas, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. the back-fin  of fishes, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8213.definition:
1. to bring forth, bear , (Homeric Hymns):—;Pass. to be delivered, bear children , (Euripides); λοχευθεῖσα πυρί, of Semele, (Euripides) 
3. Mid., just like Act., of the mother, (Euripides); of the birthplace, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. Pass., of the child, to be brought forth, born , (Sophocles Tragicus); Προμα_θεῖ λοχευθεῖσα brought to birth  by Prometheus, (Euripides): —;metaphorically, generally, to lie embedded , ἐν τεύτλοισι (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8214.definition:
1. of things, painful, distressing , Lat. molestus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. of persons, 
3. in good sense, causing sorrow  by one's departure, (Euripides) 
4. in bad sense, causing pain, troublesome, vexatious, offensive , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
5. adverb λυπηρῶς, painfully, so as to cause pain , (Sophocles Tragicus); λυπηρῶς ἔχει it is painful , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8215.definition: the border of a robe :—;Diminutive λωμάτιον, τό, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8216.definition: shortened doric form for μάτηρ, μᾶ γᾶ for μῆτερ γῆ, (Aeschulus Tragicus); μᾶ, πόθεν ἅνθρωπος; (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8218.definition:
1. a cook-shop , Lat. popina, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the place where the public cooks lived, the cooks' quarter , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8219.definition:
1. to be a cook, to cook meat , (Theophrastus Philosophus) 
2. to be a butcher , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8221.definition:
1. a cook , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. a butcher , (Euripides) (From ! μαγ, Root of μάσσω ( q. see.), because baking bread  was the business of the ancient cook.) (ML)

G8227.definition:
1. that which is learnt, a lesson , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. learning, knowledge, science , oft. in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: especially the mathematical sciences , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G8228.definition:
1. good mother, dame , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a fostermother, nurse , (Euripides):—;also a  true mother , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. a midwife , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8230.definition:
Dep. to deliver  a woman, [Refs 2nd c.AD, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
= μαιεύομαι (ML)

G8231.definition: deemed  or to be deemed happy, enviable , (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

G8232.definition: long-lived , (Aristotle Philosopher); μακροβιώτατος (Herdotus Historicus): —; οἱ M., an Ethiopian people, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8235.definition: longsuffering, patient , [variant datesAnthology Palantina: adverb -μως, (New Testament) (ML)

G8240.definition:
1. very, very much, exceedingly , (Homer), etc. 
2. strengthening the word with which it stands, μάλα πολλά very  many, (Homer); μάλα πάντες, μ. πᾶσαι, μ. πάντα, all together, every one , (Homer); μάλ᾽ ἀσκηθής all  unhurt, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀβληχρὸς μάλα τοῖος so very  weak, (Odyssey by Homer):—;so in attic, μάλα δὴ πρεσβύτης very  old, (Xenophon Historicus); μ. γέ τινες ὀλίγοι (Plato Philosophus):—;so with Advs., πάγχυ μάλα and μάλα πάγχυ quite  utterly, (Iliad by Homer); εὖ μάλα right  well, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλ᾽ αἰεί for ever and aye, (Iliad by Homer); ἄχρι μάλα κνέφαος until quite  dark, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλα διαμπερές right  through, (Iliad by Homer):—;so in attic, to express repeated action, μάλ᾽ αὖθις, μάλ᾽ αὖ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—; with Verbs, μή με μάλ᾽ αἴνεε praise me not greatly , (Iliad by Homer); ἡ δὲ μάλ᾽ ἡνιόχευεν she drove carefully , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.

(Plato Philosophus); ὡς or ὅτι μ., Lat. quam maxime, (Plato Philosophus); ὅσον μ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὡς μ. certainly , in answers, (Plato Philosophus); ὡς δύναμαι μ. (Plato Philosophus); μακρῷ μ. (Herdotus Historicus)

15. with numbers, μάλιστα means about , (Thucydides), etc.; so, ἐς μέσον μάλιστα about  the middle, (Herdotus Historicus); ἥμισυ μ. (Thucydides), etc.

5. dative feminine πεζῇ (entry ὁδῷ); as adverb, on foot , (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. by land , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8680.definition: a pirate , Lat. pirata, i. e. one who attacks  ships, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8681.definition:
1. near, hard by, close , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. absolute, χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [variant datesTragica Adespota 
4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8683.definition: to hew  or shape with an axe , Lat. dolare, (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8685.definition:
1. an axe  for felling trees, with two edges, opposite to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, (Homer) 
2. a sacrificial axe , (Homer)—;That it was not, properly, a battle axe  appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with common axes , i. e. to the last, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. in (Theophrastus Philosophus) Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean a sharp blade.  (ML)

G8688.definition: one who bears a light shield  πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer , Lat. cetratus, (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

G8689.definition:
1. a small light shield  of leather without a rim  ἴτυς); a target , Lat. cetra, originally used by the Thracians, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a body of  πελτασταί, (Euripides) 
3. a horse's ornament , (Euripides) 
4. = παλτόν, a shaft, pole , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8690.definition: a kind of axe , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8691.definition: any kind of dressed food;  but mostly in plural, pastry, cakes, sweetmeats , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8692.definition: of  or for mourning, mournful :—;adverb, πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning  for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8694.definition:
1. Dep., used in present and imperfect : 
2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 
3. to be poor  or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 
4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8695.definition:
1. five years old , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of Time, lasting five years , (Thucydides):—; neuter adverb πεντάετες, for five years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8696.definition: five cubits long  or broad , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8705.definition: the commander of fifty men , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8708.definition:
1. fiftieth , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. as Substantive, ἡ πεντηκοστή, 
3. (i.e. μερίς); at Athens the duty of one-fiftieth , or two per century , on all exports and imports, (Isaeus Orator); εὕρηκε καινὴν ἱππικῆς τινὰ πεντηκοστήν he invented a new two per century duty , in lieu of his cavalry service, i. e. paid this instead of it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. (i.e. ἡμέρα); the fiftieth day  (after the Passover), Pentecost , (New Testament) (ML)

G8709.definition:
1. ripe , Lat. maturus, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. metaphorically softened , ὀργή (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8711.definition:
1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically in vocative, mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet  ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened  pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative, ἐχθροῖς π. gentle  to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8712.definition:
1. to bring to an end, finish, accomplish, execute , [variant datesTragica Adespota, etc.:—;Pass. to be brought to an end, be finished , πάντα πεπείρανται (Odyssey by Homer): to be fulfilled, accomplished , (Euripides) etc. 
2. in speaking, to end  a discourse, finish  speaking, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. to repeat from beginning to end , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; to relate , (Euripides) 
4. absolute to effect one's purpose , especially with a negative, οὐδὲν π. to come to  no issue, do  no good, make  no progress , (Euripides) 
5. intransitive to make way, reach  or penetrate , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. intransitive to come to an end, end , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8717.definition: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

G8719.definition:
1. anything which is thrown round, a covering , (Plato Philosophus); χειρῶν περιβολαί embraces , (Euripides); so περιβολαί alone, (Xenophon Historicus); περιβολαὶ χθονός, i. e. the grave, (Euripides); π. [ ξίφεος] a scabbard, (Euripides): absolute of walls round  a town, ἑπτάπυργοι π. (Euripides) 
2. a space enclosed, compass , οἰκίης μεγάλης περιβολή a house of large compass , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a circumference, circuit , (Thucydides); π. ποιεῖσθαι to make a circuit , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. metaphorically, 
5. a compassing, endeavouring after , τῆς ἀρχῆς, Lat. affectatio imperii, (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. ἡ π. τοῦ λόγου the whole compass  of the matter, long and short  of it, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8720.definition:
1. going round, compassing, encircling , (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, περίβολος = περιβολή, ἐχίδνης περίβολοι the spires  or coils  of a serpent, (Euripides); in plural walls round a town , (Herdotus Historicus); so in singular, (Thucydides) 
3. an enclosure, circuit, compass , π. νεωρίων (Euripides); of a temple, the precincts , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8723.definition:
1. with two right hands , i.e. using both hands alike , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. very dexterous , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8724.definition: Dep. to grasp  a thing with the hand , with genitive rei, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8725.definition:
1. to be around  a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to be better than, superior to  another, surpass, excel , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer); with dative rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be superior , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage , (Thucydides) 
3. to overlive, outlive , τινι (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to survive, remain alive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;of things, to be extant, to be in existence , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. to be over and above, to remain in hand , of property, money, etc., (Thucydides); οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance  in his hands, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. to be a result  or consequence , περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . ., (Demosthenes Orator); τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have  so much hatred against me left , Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive, περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains  for you to quarrel with them, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8726.definition: a girdle round the loins, apron , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8730.definition: to be seated  or to sit all round , (Herdotus Historicus): of an army, to beleaguer, invest  a town, (Herdotus Historicus); of ships, to blockade , (Herdotus Historicus): with accusative pers. to sit down by  one, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8732.definition: to shear  or clip all round , (Herdotus Historicus); Mid., περικείρεσθαι τρίχας to have one's  hair clipt , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8736.definition:
1. to seize around, embrace , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to encompass  or surround  an enemy, so as to intercept  him, (Herdotus Historicus); μετεώρους τὰς ναῦς π. to intercept  them at sea, (Thucydides); ἐπεὰν δὲ αὐτὸν περιλάβῃς when you get hold of  him, catch  him, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be caught , οἴμοι, περιείλημμαι μόνος (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to comprehend, include , of a number of particulars, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8740.definition: to go all round , with accusative, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8741.definition:
1. a going round, a flank march , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass , τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, τὴν π. in circumference , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. γῆς π. a chart  or map  of the earth (compare πίναξ); (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. a going round in a circle, circuit , (Plutarch) 
5. of Time, a cycle  or period of time , (Pindar), etc. 
6. a prescribed course of life, system , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. a fit  of intermittent fever, (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. = περιφορά, a course at dinner , (Xenophon Historicus); π. λόγων table-talk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. the orbit of a heavenly body , (Xenophon Historicus) 
10. a well-rounded sentence, period , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8742.definition:
1. to build round , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to enclose by building round , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be built up, walled in , (Thucydides); τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure , Lat. ovile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8745.definition:
1. a walking about, walking , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a place for walking, a covered walk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. οἱ ἐκ τοῦ περιπάτου the Peripatetics, school of Aristotle , because he taught walking in a  περίπατος of the Lyceum  at Athens, (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G8746.definition:
1. to twine  or enfold round :—;Pass. to fold oneself round , with dative, ἱστῷ περιπλεχθείς (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, δίκτυον εὖ μάλα περιπλεκόμενον close folding , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to complicate, entangle , (Lucian) 
3. to wrap up in words , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8747.definition: a station for  περίπολοι, a guard-house , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8748.definition: edged with purple , π. ἐσθής a robe with a purple border , the Roman toga praetextata  or laticlavia , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8751.definition: to besprinkle all round , especially in sacred rites:—;Mid. to purify oneself , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8753.definition: dry and hard all round, exceeding hard , of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically obstinate, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8757.definition:
1. a standing round, a crowd standing round , Lat. corona, (Theophrastus Philosophus), etc. 
2. circumstances, a state of affairs , (Polybius Historicus):—;in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. outward pomp and circumstance , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8758.definition:
1. to dress, clothe, wrap up , (Pindar); ἔπηξα δ᾽ αὐτὸν εὖ περιστείλας I planted the sword having wrapt  it well with earth , i. e. planted it firmly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to dress  or lay out  a corpse, Lat. componere, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: simply, to bury , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. metaphorically to wrap up, cloak, cover , τἄδικ᾽ εὖ π. (Euripides):—;Mid., τὰ σὰ περιστέλλου κακά (Euripides) 
4. to take care of, protect, defend , (Herdotus Historicus); π. τοὺς νόμους to maintain  the laws, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ πάτρια (Demosthenes Orator); π. ἀοιδάν to uphold  minstrelsy, (Pindar) (ML)

G8762.definition:
1. to whirl round , of one preparing to throw, (Homer); π. ἵππον to wheel  it round , (Plutarch):—; Pass. to be turned round, spin round , (Iliad by Homer); π. εἰς τἀληθῆ to come round to  it, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. π. τὼ χεῖρε to tie  his hands behind  him, (Lysias Orator). (ML)

G8763.definition:
1. with pillars round the wall, surrounded with a colonnade , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, περίστυλον, ου, τό, or περίστυλος, ὁ, a peristyle, colonnade round a temple  or court-yard , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8764.definition:
1. to drag about , ἄνω καὶ κάτω (Lucian) 
2. to tear away from , τί τινος (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8765.definition:
1. to slit and tear off , (Plutarch) 
2. Pass., of a river, περισχίζεσθαι τὸν χῶρον to split round  a piece of land, i. e. split into two branches so as to surround  it, (Herdotus Historicus);—;so, of a stream of men, to part and go different ways , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8766.definition:
1. to wall all round , πλίνθοις Βαβυλῶνα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to surround with a wall , so as to beleaguer, (Thucydides) 
3. to build round , ὁ περιτετειχισμένος κύκλος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8768.definition:
1. the line round a circular body, a periphery, circumference , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the outer surface , (Plutarch) 
3. a round body , (Plutarch) 
from περιφερής (ML)

G8769.definition:
1. moving round, surrounding , with genitive, (Euripides) 
2. surrounded by , with dative, (Euripides) 
3. round, circular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of bodies, spherical, globular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of style, rounded , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8770.definition:
1. meats carried round , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. the revolving vault  of heaven, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. metaphorically, ἐν ταῖς περιφοραῖς in society , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8773.definition: to surround with a stockade , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8774.definition: exceeding joyous  or glad , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τινι at a thing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τὸ π. excessive joy , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8775.definition: to pour round  or over , τί τινι, properly of liquids, (Homer); of metal-workers, χρυσὸν κέρασιν περιχεύας having spread  gold leaf round  its horns, (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε τις χρυσὸν περιχεύεται ἀργύρῳ (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass. to be poured around , περὶ δ᾽ ἀμβρόσιος κέχυθ᾽ ὕπνος (Iliad by Homer); τῶν ὀστέων περικεχυμένων heaped all round , (Herdotus Historicus); of persons, περιχυθέντες crowding round , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8778.definition:
1. to soften, ripen  or change , by means of heat: 
2. of the sun, to ripen  fruit, (Odyssey by Homer); compare πεπαίνω. 
3. by the action of fire, to cook, dress, bake , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., πέσσεσθαι πέμματα to cook oneself  cakes, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of the stomach, to digest , like Lat. concoquere, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. metaphorically, χόλον πέσσειν to cherish  or nurse  one's wrath, Lat. fovere, (Iliad by Homer); βέλος πέσσειν to have  a dart in one to nurse , (Iliad by Homer); but in good sense, γέρα πεσσέμεν to enjoy  them, (Iliad by Homer); also, ἀκίνδυνον αἰῶνα πέσσειν to lead a sodden  life of ease, (Pindar) (ML)

G8779.definition:
1. a leaf , mostly in plural, (Homer):—; poetry, νεικέων πέταλα contentious votes (compare πεταλισμός); (Pindar) 
2. a leaf of metal , (Lucian) (ML)

G8780.definition: to spread out  sails or clothes, (Odyssey by Homer); χεῖρε πετάσσας, of one swimming, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, θυμὸν πετάσαι to open  one's heart, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., mostly in perfect, to be spread on all sides , (Homer): participle spread wide, opened wide , of folding doors, πύλαι πεπταμέναι (Iliad by Homer); πετάσθησαν (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8781.definition:
a perch  for fowls to roost at night, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8783.definition:
1. throwing stones , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, πετροβόλος, an engine for throwing stones , Lat. ballista, (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8784.definition:
1. the pine , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. any thing made from its wood, a torch of pine-wood , [variant datesTragica Adespota

G8785.definition: of  or from pine  or pine-wood , (Sophocles Tragicus); π. δάκρυα tears of the pine , i. e. the resinous drops that ooze from it, (Euripides) (ML)

G8787.definition:
1. anything joined together, framework , of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Lat. pegma, a moveable scaffold used in theatres, (Juvenal) 
2. metaphorically, π. γενναίως παγέν a bond  in honour bound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. π. τῆς χιόνος frozen  snow, (Polybius Historicus) 
 (ML)

G8788.definition:
1. to leap, spring, bound , ὑψόσε ποσσὶν ἐπήδα (Iliad by Homer); π. ἐς σκάφος (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative cognate, πήδημα πηδᾶν to take  a leap, (Euripides); with accusative loci, πεδία πηδᾶν to bound over  them, (Sophocles Tragicus); π. πλάκα (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer); of the heart, to leap, throb , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; of sudden changes, τί πηδᾶις εἰς ἄλλους τρόπου; (Euripides) (ML)

G8789.definition: of clay , Lat. fictilis, οἱ πήλινοι clay figures , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8790.definition:
1. to make fat, fatten , (Euripides); π. χθόνα to fatten  the soil, of a dead man, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to be  or become fat , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. metaphorically, 
3. to increase, enlarge , πλοῦτον (Pindar)

G8791.definition:
an ape, monkey , (Aristophanes Comicus); as feminine, πίθηκος μήτηρ (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;of persons, an ape, jackanapes , (Aristophanes Comicus)

G8797.definition: the pine, stone pine , (Homer):—;proverbial, πίτυος τρόπον ἐκτρίβεσθαι to be destroyed like a pine , i. e. utterly , because the pine when cut down never grows again, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8798.definition:
1. neuter πῖον, genitive πίονος, fat, plump , Lat. pinguis, (Homer); π. δημός rich  fat, (Iliad by Homer); of oil, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of soil, fat, rich.  (Iliad by Homer); also, πίονα ἔργα pingues segetes , (Iliad by Homer); ὀπώρας πίων ποτός, of wine, (Sophocles Tragicus)

G8799.definition: to turn sideways  or aside , πλ. πρὸς τοὺς ἀντίους ἀνέμους (i.e. τὴν ναῦν); to beat up  against adverse winds, (Lucian): metaphorically, πλ. ἢ φωνὴν ἢ πρᾶξιν to adapt  them to circumstances , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8800.definition:
1. placed sideways, slanting, aslant , Lat. obliquus, (Thucydides) 
2. πλάγια, ων, τά, the sides , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in military sense, τοῖς πλαγίοις ἐπιέναι to attack the flanks , (Thucydides); εἰς τὰ πλ. παράγειν or παραπέμπειν to make an army file off right and left , (Xenophon Historicus); πλαγίους λαβεῖν τοὺς πολεμίους to take the enemy in flank , (Xenophon Historicus)

4. metaphorically not straightforward, crooked, treacherous , φρένες (Pindar); πλάγια φρονεῖν (Euripides) (ML)

G8801.definition: a making to wander, a dispersing , τῶν νεῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8802.definition:
the oriental plane , Lat. platanus, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
From πλατύς, because of its broad leaves.  (ML)

G8804.definition: mostly, most often, very often , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8805.definition: more frequently, oftener , (Plato Philosophus): several times, frequently , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8809.definition:
1. an advantage, gain, privilege , (Plato Philosophus): in plural gains, successes , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. an act of overreaching, selfish trick , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8810.definition:
1. a rib : mostly in plural the ribs, the side , (Iliad by Homer), etc.;—;also in singular, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν the side  of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right flank  (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8811.definition:
a mistake in music, false note : metaphorically a fault, offence, error , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πλημμελέω (ML)

G8812.definition: to make a false note in music : metaphorically to go wrong, offend, err , τι in a thing, (Euripides), etc.; εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος to be ill-treated  by one, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8815.definition:
1. a filling up, filling , (Plato Philosophus): often of eating and drinking, satiety , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. the completion of a number , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8816.definition:
1. near, close to , with genitive or dative, πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—;absolute near, neighbouring , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;as Substantive a neighbour , ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. adverb πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας, near, nigh, hard by , with genitive, (Homer), etc.; with dative, (Euripides) 
3. with the Art., ὁ πλησίον (i.e. ὤν); one's neighbour , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; so in doric, ὁ πλα_τίον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;also, with Substantives, ὁ πλ. παράδεισος (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. comparative πλησιαίτερος, Sup. -αίτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)—;comparative adverb πλησιαιτέρω, (Herdotus Historicus); -αίτερον, (Xenophon Historicus); Sup. -αίτατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8818.definition:
1. to make into bricks , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to make bricks , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 
2. to build of brick , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to make in the form of a plinth  or brick , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 (ML)

G8819.definition:
1. a small brick , (Thucydides) 
2. = πλαίσιον, a rectangle  or square , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8820.definition: a brick , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat. ducere lateres, to make bricks , (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν to bake  them, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8822.definition:
1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically the complication of  a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8824.definition:
1. floating , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί swimmers , i. e. fish, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. navigable , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of seasons, fit for navigation , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8827.definition: the organ of  breathing, the lungs , Lat. pulmo, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural, [variant datesTragica Adespota; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

G8828.definition:
1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8829.definition:
1. to long for, yearn after  what is absent, to miss  or regret  what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with infinitive to be anxious  to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs  to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing  soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.definition:
1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.definition:
1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a  χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to embroider  a robe, (Pindar), etc. 
3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.definition:
1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 
3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.definition: of  or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.definition:
1. wool  in its raw state, a fleece , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: a lock  or tuft of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. proverbial in heterocl. accusative of 3rd declension, εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an ass shearing , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.definition:
1. of  or for war , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises , (Thucydides) 
3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. the military class , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. of persons, skilled in war, warlike , (Thucydides), etc. 
6. like an enemy, stirring up hostility , (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb, πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be hostile , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.definition:
1. of  or belonging to war , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. of  or like an enemy, hostile , (Pindar), etc.:—;as Substantive an enemy , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility , (Thucydides) 
3. generally, opposed, adverse , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of  or from the enemy , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά, enemy's wares, contraband , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα); the enemy's country , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. adverb -ίως, in hostile manner , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.definition:
1. a warrior, combatant , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.definition:
1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.definition:
1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.definition:
1. gray, grizzled, grisly , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. mostly of hair, gray  or hoary  from age, (Homer); πολιοί gray-haired men , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;absolute, αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the gray hairs  come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών an old man's  tear, (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically hoary, venerable , (Euripides) 
4. like λευκός, bright, clear, serene , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.definition:
1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.definition:
1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 
2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8860.definition:
1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient , (Homeric Hymns) 
2. lasting for long , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.definition: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.definition:
1. in early Greek only as Dep. 
2. absolute to work hard, do work, suffer toil , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο were busied  about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους was busy  with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. metaphorically to be in distress, to distress oneself , (Iliad by Homer):—; to suffer, be sick , (Thucydides) 
4. with accusative to work hard at, to make  or do with pains  or care , (Homer) 
5. after (Homer), the active form prevails 
6. intransitive to toil, labour , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π. to labour  in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει do  not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. with accusative cognate, π. πόνον, μόχθους to go through, suffer  them, [variant datesTragica Adespota; also with accusative partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
8. absolute to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer , (Thucydides): to be worn out, spoilt , (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. Pass., impersonal, οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 
10. transitive, 
11. with accusative pers. to afflict, distress , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be worn out, to suffer greatly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
12. Pass., also, to be trained  or educated , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
13. with accusative rei, like ἐκπονεῖν, to gain by toil  or labour , χρήματα (Xenophon Historicus): Pass. to be won  or achieved by toil , (Pindar) (ML)

G8863.definition: Dep. to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue , (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8864.definition:
to pass the sea , νῆυς ποντοποροῦσα sea-sailing , (Odyssey by Homer) 
from ποντοπόρος (ML)

G8866.definition: a house of ill-fame, brothel , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8867.definition: of  or for harlots , π. τέλος the tax paid by brothel-keepers , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8869.definition:
1. a purple garment  or covering , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a red-coloured bird , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8874.definition: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8876.definition: a selling, sale , ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic dative) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for sale , (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8879.definition:
1. to make soft, mild  or gentle, to soften, soothe, calm , (Hesiod), etc.; πρ. ἕλκος to soothe  a raging sore, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τινὰ λόγοις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to become soft  or gentle, grow milder , (Herdotus Historicus); of passion, to abate , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to tame  wild animals, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8880.definition:
1. a gift of honour , such as was offered to elders, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the privilege of age , and generally, a privilege , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. the right of the eldest, his share of the inheritance , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8881.definition:
1. an old man , Lat. senex, (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος, the elder , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;plural πρέσβεις, elders , always implying dignity, chiefs, princes , (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 
2. (Homer) uses only the comparative and Sup., comparative πρεσβύτερος, α, ον, elder, older , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἐνιαυτῷ by a year, (Aristophanes Comicus); βουλαὶ πρεσβύτεραι the wise  councils of age , (Pindar);—;Sup. πρεσβύτατος, η, ον, eldest , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: —;the comparative and Sup. were used of things, πρεσβύτερόν τι (or οὐδὲν); ἔχειν = Lat. aliquid (or nihil) antiquius habere, to deem higher, more important , τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πρεσβύτερα ποιεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν (Herdotus Historicus); πρεσβύτατον κρίνειν τι (Thucydides); πρεσβυτέρως γυμναστικὴν μουσικῆς τετιμηκέναι more highly than . . , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, merely of magnitude, πρεσβύτερον κακὸν κακοῦ one evil greater than  another, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. like πρεσβευτής, an ambassador , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;plural πρέσβεις is more used than πρεσβευταί, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
4. a chief, president : comparative πρεσβύτερος, an elder of the Jewish Council , (New Testament), etc.: an elder of the Church, presbyter , (New Testament) (ML)

G8882.definition:
1. to blow up, swell out by blowing , ἔπρησεν δ᾽ ἄνεμος μέσον ἱστίον (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to blow out, drive out by blowing , τὸ δ᾽ [ αἷμα] ἀνὰ στόμα πρῆσε he blew  a shower of blood through his mouth, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8883.definition:
1. to have  a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase , (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with  one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by  his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically, οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι to buy at  no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον to buy  it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to farm  a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8886.definition:
1. a choosing  one thing before  another, an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; κατὰ προαίρεσιν on purpose, as one will , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. a purpose, plan , or scope  of action, a course of life, principle  of action, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. in political language, a deliberate course of action, a policy , (Demosthenes Orator):—;also, a mode  of government, such as an oligarchy, (Demosthenes Orator); in plural, τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public principles, your general policy , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. a department of government , (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. a political party , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8890.definition: the space immediately in front of  or round a town, a suburb , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8891.definition: property in cattle  πρόβατα); cattle , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8892.definition:
1. anything projecting, a headland, promontory , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus); προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen armour  of horses, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with genitive a defence against  a thing, πέτρων (Aeschulus Tragicus); χείματος (Euripides); κακῶν (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame as a defence , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. anything put forward as an excuse  or screen , (Demosthenes Orator); so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make a stalking horse  of him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. that which is proposed, a task, business , (Euripides) 
7. a problem  in Geometry, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8894.definition:
1. to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do  a thing, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; also πρ. ὅπως (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. absolute to shew zeal, exert oneself , (Herdotus Historicus):—; to be of good cheer , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with accusative rei, to be eager  or zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G8895.definition:
1. the front-door, the door leading from the  αὐλή, (Homer); also in plural, (Homer) 
2. the space before a door , a kind of porch  or verandah , Lat. vestibulum, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 
3. metaphorically, Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος (Pindar); πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8896.definition:
1. to send before, send on  or forward , (Homer): also, to send  something to  another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to send away, dismiss, let go , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let  her go  to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop  a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let  the helm slip  from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides) 
4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot  or dart forth , (Homer) 
5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours  its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer) 
6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow  one to do, (Pindar) 
7. to give up, deliver over, betray  one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass. to be given  or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up  or devote  oneself to present delights, (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of sounds, to utter , (Aeschines Orator), etc. 
10. to give up, let go: to give up  to the enemy, (Thucydides), etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave  themselves up as lost , (Thucydides) 
11. to desert, abandon , (Thucydides); οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς did  not lose  themselves (i. e. take bribes), (Demosthenes Orator) 
12. to give away, give freely , (Thucydides), etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων (Demosthenes Orator) 
13. to throw off  one's clothes, (Demosthenes Orator): and, in bad sense, to throw away , τὸν καιρόν (Demosthenes Orator); τὰ πατρῷα (Aeschines Orator): absolute to be lavish , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer  us to be wronged, (Thucydides); προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι (Xenophon Historicus); πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι (Demosthenes Orator) 
15. to suffer to escape , (Polybius Historicus) 
16. rarely in good sense, to give over  to one, confide to one's care , (Xenophon Historicus) 
17. to neglect, disregard , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; absolute to neglect all advice, to be reckless , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8897.definition:
1. to set before;  so in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Pass., with aorist2  and perfect active, φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8898.definition:
1. to seize beforehand, preoccupy , (Thucydides), etc.:—;Pass. to be preoccupied , (Thucydides) 
2. metaphorically to anticipate, frustrate , (Thucydides):—;of persons, to anticipate  or surprise  them, (Thucydides) 
3. to overpower before , (Thucydides) (ML)
